result.summary:
ISS-0329 comparison: distinct mechanism, not a recurrence. ISS-0329 was a hardcoded-literal unique-constraint collision (tenants.idp_realm_id) hit on Repo.insert! -- resolved by switching a hardcoded realm string to unique_realm/1. ISS-0343's symptom is 'relation tenant_*.event_type_registry does not exist', a DDL-visibility error (the schema/table was dropped or never existed at query time), not a constraint violation. Both are 'test-isolation defects that surface only under parallel execution', which is why they look similar at a glance, but the underlying fault classes differ: ISS-0329 was a naming collision between two inserts; ISS-0343 is a race between a query against a tenant schema and that schema's DROP.

Mechanism reasoning (from code alone, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex + test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs): scripts/test_parallel.sh's N partitions are separate OS processes/BEAM VMs with independent connection pools, so a CROSS-PROCESS explanation (one partition's Sandbox.mode flip affecting another partition's connections) is implausible -- there is no shared BEAM state between partitions, only the shared physical Postgres cluster. The plausible WITHIN-A-SINGLE-PARTITION mechanism is a real race, not a naming collision: TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 calls Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) and, per its own moduledoc/INV-F-6, deliberately never restores :manual. This flips the sandbox mode for the ENTIRE connection pool of that partition process, for the rest of that partition's run -- not just for the calling test. ExUnit runs async:true test modules concurrently with (not serially before/after) any async:false module such as BackfillTest, all sharing that one process's connection pool. Once any test in the partition has flipped to :auto (BackfillTest itself, or an earlier-adopted-fixture test in the same partition, e.g. promotion_test.exs/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs, both named in the fixture moduledoc as adopters), every test in that partition loses per-test transactional isolation for the remainder of the run: writes are real, committed, and visible across connections/tests. Tenant/schema names are already collision-proofed (TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug), so this is not a same-name collision. Instead, BackfillTest's downgrade_to_v1!/1 and Backfill.run/2's underlying queries operate against schema_name/tenant_id captured at fixture-provision time; TenantFixture's own teardown runs DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "<schema>" CASCADE from an on_exit callback whose scheduling relative to other concurrently-running async tests' on_exit callbacks is not synchronized by anything in this file. If Backfill.run (per its moduledoc, a module-level backfill sequenced by ISS-0332's design, not obviously scoped to a single tenant_id -- it is invoked here with only v2_attrs(), no tenant_id argument) enumerates/touches more than the fixture's own just-provisioned tenant, or if ExUnit's own test scheduling interleaves this test's queries with a *different*, concurrently-running async test's teardown DROP SCHEMA CASCADE against a schema that Backfill.run is mid-query against, the query fails with exactly the observed 'relation ... does not exist' -- the schema was real when queried and gone by the time the query executed, a genuine DDL race enabled by :auto mode's lack of transactional isolation, not a name collision.

One real scripts/test_parallel.sh run (executed exactly once, N=8 via nproc, this sandbox's resource limits given): 'test_parallel: N=8 (source: nproc) ... combined: 1045 tests, 3 properties, 2 failures (1046/1048 passed)'. Per-partition: partition 1: 257 tests/0 failures/exit 0; partition 2: crashed before any test ran (Mix.Error: 'The database for Letflow.Repo couldn't be created: killed', preceded by a DBConnection.Ownership.ownership_checkout timeout during ecto.migrate -- this sandbox's Postgres connection budget, not ISS-0343); partition 3: 196 tests/2 failures/exit 2 -- failures were 'Mix.Tasks.Letflow.SeedTest AC2 ...' (DBConnection.ConnectionError: connection checkout timeout after 5300ms, again a pool-exhaustion symptom of this constrained sandbox) and 'Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest ISS-0060 ...' -- neither is BackfillTest and neither mentions event_type_registry; partition 4: 306 tests/0 failures/exit 0; partition 5: 286 tests/0 failures/exit 0; partitions 6/7/8: crashed before any test ran with Postgrex FATAL 53300 'too_many_connections' during ecto.create, again this sandbox's connection-limit ceiling under 8-way parallelism, unrelated to the BackfillTest mechanism. grep across all four completed partitions' logs for 'event_type_registry does not exist' and for 'BackfillTest' found zero matches. Conclusion: did not reproduce in this one real attempt, consistent with a low-frequency intermittent -- the prior PR #659 run already showed BackfillTest failing once with exactly this error (4 failures), so the failure mode is real even though this single attempt (partly starved of usable partitions by this sandbox's own connection-count ceiling, an orthogonal environment constraint) did not trigger it. No follow-up runs performed, per the handoff's bound.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER: design a fix that removes the cross-test blast radius of Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) rather than chasing a specific interleaving. Concretely: (a) confirm/scope Letflow.TenantProvisioning.Backfill.run/1's query surface -- if it operates across ALL tenants in the database rather than the one tenant_id the calling test just provisioned, that is the actual defect to fix (scope it to a single tenant, or have BackfillTest assert against a schema-isolated/dedicated tenant set so a concurrent test's DROP SCHEMA CASCADE on an unrelated tenant can never intersect its query), and/or (b) reduce the window in which the DROP SCHEMA CASCADE in TenantFixture.teardown/2 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex ~L334) can race a concurrently-running :auto-mode query from another test in the same partition -- e.g. take the same per-tenant advisory/row lock TenantProvisioning already uses at provision time (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(schema_name)), visible in the partition-3 log) around the DROP as well, so a query in flight against that schema is serialized against its own teardown rather than racing it. Do not attempt a naming-collision fix (TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug already collision-proofs names) -- the mechanism here is a DDL-vs-query race enabled by global :auto sandbox mode, not a duplicate identifier.
